LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERNS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when, where, whose, who and what) sentences, 1. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity
2. use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication
3. respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERNS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERNS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity

What this means
In this part you learn to identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns to a partner. (skill: use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity.
3. Practise this skill: use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication.
4. Practise this skill: respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when, where, whose, who and what) sentences, 1. Why do we ask questions?
2. Which words do we use to ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity.
5. Be able to: use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
